Confidence Intervals for the Ratio of Two Poisson Rates

Source: R/poissonDiffCI.R
poissonRatioCI.Rd

Computes a confidence interval for the ratio \((x_1/n_1) / (x_2/n_2)\) of two independent Poisson rates.

poissonRatioCI(
  x1,
  n1 = 1,
  x2,
  n2 = 1,
  conf.level = 0.95,
  sides = c("two.sided", "left", "right"),
  method = c("exact", "midp", "wald-log")
)

Arguments

x1

number of events in the first sample

n1

time base for the first event count

x2

number of events in the second sample

n2

time base for the second event count

conf.level

confidence level, defaults to 0.95

sides

a character string specifying the side of the confidence interval, one of "two.sided" (default), "left" or "right"

method

character string specifying the method, one of "exact" (default), "midp" or "wald-log"

Value

If recycling yields a single case, a named numeric vector with elements est, lci and uci. Otherwise a data frame with one row per case, whose first three columns are est, lci and uci and whose remaining columns contain the recycled argument values.

Details

"exact" (default) conditions on the total count: given \(x_1 + x_2\), the count \(x_1\) is binomial with success probability \(n_1\theta/(n_1\theta + n_2)\), so a Clopper-Pearson interval for that probability maps directly to one for the rate ratio \(\theta\). This is the construction underlying poisson.test for two samples. "midp" replaces the Clopper-Pearson limits by their mid-p counterparts, which are shorter and closer to nominal coverage at the cost of exactness. "wald-log" is the asymptotic interval symmetric on the log scale and is undefined when either count is zero, in which case \((0, \infty)\) is returned.

Arguments are recycled to a common length. sides names the side carrying the finite limit, and since the ratio is bounded below by zero the open end of a one-sided interval is reported as 0 or Inf rather than as \(\pm\infty\).

References

Sahai, H., Khurshid, A. (1993) Confidence intervals for the ratio of two Poisson means. The Mathematical Scientist, 18, 43-50.

Graham, P. L., Mengersen, K., Morton, A. P. (2003) Confidence limits for the ratio of two rates based on likelihood scores. Statistics in Medicine, 22(12), 2071-2083.

See also

poissonCI, poissonDiffCI, binomRatioCI, poisson.test

Other ci.proportion: binomCI(), binomDiffCI(), binomRatioCI(), multinomCI(), poissonCI(), poissonDiffCI()

Examples

## 15 events in 100 person-years against 6 events in 120 person-years
poissonRatioCI(15, 100, 6, 120)
#>      est      lci      uci 
#> 3.000000 1.099947 9.437411 
## [1] est 3.000000 lci 1.099947 uci 9.437411

## agrees with the two-sample conditional test in stats
poisson.test(c(15, 6), c(100, 120))$conf.int
#> [1] 1.099947 9.437411
#> attr(,"conf.level")
#> [1] 0.95

poissonRatioCI(15, 100, 6, 120, method = "midp")
#>      est      lci      uci 
#> 3.000000 1.188883 8.415485
